newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-Banks eye top borrowers.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-Banks eye top borrowers.

text.p: Choice names like Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, the Airport Authority and China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd are tipped to be considering fundraisings, bankers said.
"There is going to be a lot of interesting deals," said a banker from a major local financial institution.

Hutchison is tipped to be seeking up to HK$10 billion, a refinancing of an earlier loan at lower rates, bankers said. Banks are also hoping for another deal from the Airport Authority (AA), which last year signed a stunningly successful HK$8.2 billion loan, which attracted almost 50 banks. Bankers said a loan would probably be earmarked for a second runway at Chek Lap Kok, which could cost up to HK$4 billion.
However, the AA might opt to raise some money through a debt issuance facility arranged and operated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).
The HKMA has been encouraging public bodies like the AA and the Mass Transit Railway Corp to issue debt securities to increase liquidity and establish a new pricing benchmark.
China Everbright, which surprised the market earlier this month by buying into Hong Kong Telecommunications Holdings Ltd, is also believed to be seeking funds, bankers said.

China Everbright was discussing funding its HK$11.4 billion purchase of 7.74 percent of Hongkong Telecom, they said. China Everbright has to make payment by June 3. While China Everbright has been overshadowed by more successful mainland red chips like CITIC Pacific Ltd, it has good connections with the Chinese government.
China Everbright is also the parent of China Everbright International Ltd, China Everbright Technology Ltd and China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd.
Its banking arm, Everbright Bank of China, is also in the market with a US$64 million floating rate note.
Another mainland bank, China Merchant Bank, on Monday mandated SBC Warburg to arrange a US$100 million floating-rate note issue, bankers said.
The facility has a final maturity of seven years with a put option in year five. It will be priced at par to float at 70 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
General syndication is expected to start in mid June.
More details have emerged on a loan by a Swire Properties Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd joint venture, which is expected to be for four years, bankers said.
Pricing was between 50 and 60 basis points, they said.
Details have emerged on the Arvind Mills Ltd seven year floating-rate certificate of deposit issue.

It carries a coupon of 130 basis points over LIBOR and was issued at par, and does not have any puts or call options. Siam City Cement Public Co Ltd's term loan facility has been increased to US$81 million from US$75 million, bankers said.
China Merchant Holding Co Ltd's US$200 million financing facility has been allotted, bankers said.
The first three years consisted of a US commercial paper programme combined with a revolving credit facility and the remaining two years will be a term loan facility, it said.
AMMB International (Labuan) Ltd launched a three-year US$100 million FRCD at par with a coupon of 25 basis points over LIBOR.
Co-lead managers get an all-in of 29.5 basis points for US$5 million, and managers an all-in of 28 basis points for US$3 million to US$4 million.
